queries.query: Plotinus on turning the gaze inward and laboring at one's own soul the way a craftsman perfects a figure, removing what is superfluous until the inner splendor shows
queries.note: The self-sculpting passage of the treatise on Beauty; 'withdraw into yourself', 'statue', 'sculptor', 'chisel' paraphrased into craftsman imagery; 'Plotinus' kept as the author's name.

queries.query: the philosopher's account of repeatedly awakening out of his body into himself, identified with the divine order, and then puzzling over how the soul ever comes down again
queries.note: The famous opening of the treatise on the soul's descent; 'lifted out of the body', 'self-encentered', 'marvellous beauty' paraphrased away.

queries.query: why Plotinus calls every virtue a purification, comparing the embodied soul to a precious metal dulled by clinging earth that regains its beauty only when refined back to itself alone
queries.note: 'Gold degraded when mixed with earthy particles', 'gold with gold alone', 'moral-discipline' paraphrased into refining imagery; Plotinus kept.

queries.query: the defense of consecrated images and holy places: the wise of old prepared receptacles tuned to the soul of the All so that a divine presence would settle in them
queries.note: The shrines-and-statues passage; 'erection of shrines and statues', 'tractable', 'mirror' paraphrased away.

queries.query: how can love of beautiful things become a ladder toward the divine
queries.note: The ascent from sensible to intelligible beauty; eros as a path upward is answered across many traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: why does a good and provident source produce a world that contains inferior and ugly things
queries.note: Against the censurers of the Kosmos: gradation of primals to ultimates; theodicy is pan-traditional. No target — graded post-hoc.
